sources.title: How we hire | Uber Careers
sources.basis: Uber's own careers page describing its hiring process end to end (uber.com/us/en/careers/interviewing/ 301-redirects here)
sources.summary: Six-step process: application; a Talent Team conversation on experience, role fit and working conditions; a Hiring Manager chat on skills and decision-making; a Technical Interview for tech roles (collaborative real-time problem solving assessing coding and building capability); a role-dependent Functional Exercise/Assessment (analytics challenges, written exercises, portfolio reviews, work simulations); and a Team Interview with teammates and cross-functional partners on collaboration and decision-making.

sources.title: FAQ - Careers at Airbnb
sources.basis: Airbnb's own careers FAQ page describing its interview process
sources.summary: States the interview process 'is both rigorous and fun', that depending on role it 'may involve taking a test, making a video, or joining us for an event', that candidates meet with multiple individuals on the current team, that Airbnb aims to respond within 3-4 weeks of application, and that recruiters correspond only from @airbnb.com or @ext.airbnb.com and never ask for financial/payment information during interviewing. Thin on round-by-round detail.

sources.title: Clear Interview Process and Insider Insights | Databricks
sources.basis: Databricks' own careers page on its interview process
sources.summary: Seven-stage journey (identify opportunities, apply, connect with Talent Acquisition, skill assessments, interviewing, reference checks, decision/offer) typically spanning two to three months. Structure: recruiter call, then a pre-onsite screen (hiring-manager screen, technical assessment, or skill evaluation), then an onsite loop of four to six interviews, with a presentation stage for some go-to-market/executive roles. All interviews conducted virtually via Google Meet. Emphasises behavioural questions using real-life past examples ('Tell me about a time...').

sources.title: Hiring Process | Snowflake Careers
sources.basis: Snowflake's own careers page on its hiring process
sources.summary: Three-stage general process (apply, interview, decide) with reference and background checks before offer. Engineering-specific pathway of four stages over 2-4 weeks: a 30-minute initial screen with recruiter/hiring manager on technical background and role fit; 60-minute technical interviews with live coding and system design; a panel of 3-5 sessions of 60 minutes each covering technical skills, behavioural fit and collaboration, sometimes including a 30-minute tech-talk presentation; then a decision within days. Candidates not hearing back within 30 days should assume no match.

sources.title: Hiring Process | Intuit Careers
sources.basis: Intuit's own careers page on its hiring process for engineering-style roles
sources.summary: Five-stage process: Interview Set-Up (engineers download coding tools and solve a technical question alone to present at the onsite craft demo); Craft Demonstration (60 minutes, 4 hiring-team members - candidate shares accomplishments with visual aids then completes a role-relevant case study); Assessors Interview (45 minutes, 2 assessors on technical skills and the case study); Team Member Interview (30 minutes, 1 cross-functional colleague on Intuit values and team dynamics); Manager Interview (30-60 minutes on career motivation and development). Commits to feedback within 24 hours of interviewing.

sources.title: Interviewing at Pinterest | Pinterest Careers
sources.basis: Pinterest's own careers page on its interview process
sources.summary: Four phases: Application Review; Initial Conversations (a recruiter call on experience and process overview, then a hiring-manager conversation on qualifications and the team); a Team Interview round of competency-based interviews with team members and stakeholders; Decision & Offer (team debriefs after all interviews, recruiter communicates outcome). Interviews are described as structured around competencies rather than a fixed format, evaluating both technical qualifications and cross-functional fit.

sources.title: Advice from Pinterest Recruiting | Pinterest Careers
sources.basis: Pinterest's own careers blog, advice from five named Pinterest recruiters on its interview process
sources.summary: Five Pinterest recruiters (Patrice Williams, Victoria Perez, Juliana Chua, Philip Floyd, Adam Gorelick) describe what they look for: treating the interview as a mutual exchange with questions welcomed; reviewing the job description and preparing an example per requirement; testing video-conferencing equipment beforehand and asking clarifying questions; researching interviewers on LinkedIn; and for technical roles, clearly communicating problem-solving approach and speaking concisely about impact.

sources.title: How we hire | Dropbox Careers
sources.basis: Dropbox's own careers page on its hiring process
sources.summary: Five stages: Online Application (AI helps surface relevant skills/experience but humans decide advancement); Initial Screen (recruiter discusses experience, interests and goals; AI transcription may be used with consent); Assessment or Technical Screen (a skills-based exercise, candidates notified in advance if AI tools are involved and may decline); Virtual Interviews (all interviews on video, discussing strengths, working style and approach to collaboration); Final Review and Decision (human judgement drives the decision, feedback given to finalists). Emphasises hiring for 'durable skills' - critical thinking, adaptability, curiosity, connection, judgment.
